mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals an economic slowdown, leading to reduced corporate earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a tightening monetary policy amid a strong labor market, which typically precedes a market correction due to rising borrowing costs and recession risks, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high housing starts (HOUST > 1100 thousand units) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 470,000 million dollars), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches a peak and the risk of a downturn increases, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 470000, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates higher corporate profits from increased manufacturing output.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers a hawkish monetary policy response and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During an overheating labor market (UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 150,000 jobs per month), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 150000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 2.0% indicates a robust economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 > 2.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
